name: Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity / Star Number
details: False for finite binary classes with identification stopping and no final confirmation query. On singletons plus the empty concept on $n$ coordinates, proper equivalence-query complexity is one while star number is $n$. Thus the asserted domination fails for every $n\ge2$, and no finite-valued function of proper equivalence-query complexity bounds star number on all finite classes.
proof_source: Survey Remark rem:proper-query-teaching-separation gives the full witness proof; database values 112 and 18 give its endpoints. Parameter 25 specifies stopping and acceptance. The original rejected record is preserved at sync/query_protocol_corrections/originals/387_proper_equivalence_queries_complexity_star_number.json.
witness_verification: For the same finite class on $n\ge2$ coordinates, parameter 1 is $1$ and parameter 2 is $n$ (values 112 and 18). Parameter 2 divided by one plus parameter 1 tends to infinity, refuting the stated direction and every same-direction affine bound. The first parameter stays fixed, so these witnesses also refute any same-direction finite-valued functional bound.
